newsitem.title: USA: Bombardier eyes flight speed record.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier eyes flight speed record.

text.p: Bombardier Aerospace, a unit of Canadian conglomerate Bombardier Inc, plans to set the Pittsburgh-to-Paris speed record this week with its Learjet 60 business jet and will challenge its competitors to break it, Bombardier officials said Wednesday.

"What we're attempting is to establish a record and we'll challenge our competitors to beat it," said Robert Agostino, director of Bombardier's Learjet flight operations and the pilot who will make the flight along with a co-pilot.
"The Learjet 60 is only three years old and we're trying to establish (more awareness of it) in the marketplace," Agostino said at a news conference.

Bombardier officials said the plane, certified in 1993, already has captured one-third of the business jet market but they are hoping the transatlantic flight, a distance of 3,452 nautical miles, will boost its market share.
Bombardier's main competitors in business jets are Raytheon Co and Cessna, a privately-held manufacturer.
Traveling from 507 to 509 miles per hour, the Learjet 60 will depart Pittsburgh on Thursday and stop in Gander, Newfoundland, to refuel, approximately two hours and 35 minutes after takeoff.
The jet will then take slightly over five hours to reach Paris, Agostino said. The plane will fly at an altitude of 43,000 feet to avoid interfering with commercial air traffic.
Bombardier plans to demonstrate the jet next week at the 1997 Paris Air Show.

Michael Graff, president of Bombardier's business aircraft unit, said the Learjet 60's capability to travel up to 522 miles per hour enables it to make the Pittsburgh-to-Paris flight at least 30 minutes faster than its competitors.
Additionally, he said the plane's rippled fuselage design makes it highly aerodynamic and able to fly at higher speeds than other mid-size business jets.
The plane is powered by twin turbofan engines and consumes about 1,100 pounds of fuel per hour. It holds a crew of two and up to ten passengers.
